text: Some doors are sealed because what is behind them is dangerous.
speaker: False Scribe
note: Nervousness gone; suddenly older. Slower, calmer, lower.

text: Zik waited.
speaker: Narrator

text: The scribe's eyes dropped to the mark on Zik's palm.
speaker: Narrator

text: Some are sealed because the thing behind them is still waiting.
speaker: False Scribe
note: Nervousness gone; suddenly older. Slower, calmer, lower.

text: Then he walked away.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik remained in the alley.
speaker: Narrator

text: The words should have sounded like a threat. Instead they sounded familiar. He hated that.
speaker: Narrator

text: When Zik returned to his mother's house to gather the last of his gear, he found the second wrong thing.
speaker: Narrator

text: The door was locked.
speaker: Narrator

text: The crack in the frame was exactly where he had left it. Nothing looked disturbed.
speaker: Narrator

text: That was the problem.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik stood in the hallway for nearly a minute without entering.
speaker: Narrator

text: His father had taught him to notice things that were about to fail. He had also taught him that a room could tell you when someone had been inside it. A moved object. A displaced grain of dust. A door closed with the wrong amount of force.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik pushed the door open.
speaker: Narrator

text: The room was dark.
speaker: Narrator

text: His mother was asleep.
speaker: Narrator

text: The small clay tablet he used as a weight for papers was on the table. It had been beside the window.
speaker: Narrator

text: His spare knife was beneath his pallet. It had been on the shelf.
speaker: Narrator

text: His father's measuring cord still hung beside the doorway.
speaker: Narrator

text: Bel-iddin had always coiled it clockwise.
speaker: Narrator

text: Someone had hung it back the other way.
speaker: Narrator

text: Nobody else would have noticed.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik did.
speaker: Narrator

text: And the loose brick behind which he kept emergency coin was slightly askew.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik closed the door behind him.
speaker: Narrator

text: He did not wake his mother.
speaker: Narrator

text: He crossed the room and crouched beside the wall. The brick had been replaced carefully. Too carefully. He pulled it free.
speaker: Narrator

text: The emergency coins were still there. He counted them anyway.
speaker: Narrator

text: One. Two. Three.
speaker: Narrator

text: All present.
speaker: Narrator

text: He put them back and examined the brick. A small smear of pale dust marked one edge. Someone had removed it. Someone had put it back. Someone had been careful enough to leave the money untouched.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik sat on the edge of his pallet for a long moment.
speaker: Narrator

text: His mother breathed softly in her sleep. The kiln beneath the house gave a low, constant rumble. The room was warm. Familiar. Safe.
speaker: Narrator

text: The word was ridiculous.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik looked at the journal in his hands.
speaker: Narrator

text: The mark on his palm throbbed in time with his heartbeat. He had lied to the Collector. But the Collector had already known he was lying. That was the part Zik couldn't fit into the arithmetic.
speaker: Narrator

text: A lie was a transaction. You gave someone a falsehood and received something in return: information, time, distance, safety.
speaker: Narrator

text: But the Collector had not been negotiating with him. He had been waiting.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik opened the journal. The pages were blank. He turned to the map.
speaker: Narrator

text: The vertical section was still there. The rivers. The impossible structures. The spiral descending through the layers of the world.
speaker: Narrator

text: At the bottom of the map, beneath the words I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE DEPTH, there was now a second line.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik stared at it.
speaker: Narrator

text: He had not seen it before.
speaker: Narrator

text: The handwriting was his father's.
speaker: Narrator

text: I WAS WRONG ABOUT WHO WAS LOOKING.
speaker: Bel-iddin
note: New line in Bel-iddin's hand, still wet.

text: He read it twice.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then a third time.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not because he doubted the words.
speaker: Narrator

text: Because he was trying to remember whether they had existed a heartbeat earlier.
speaker: Narrator
